rows.reason: Lines 7-9 give the bag to soles coming off; each distractor's execution checks (line 8 second box/charity, line 5 smell); hint points at the three rules without naming the key.

Execution on 'Both show he has not been listening' says 'He answers each time', which contradicts the key's own premise that his replies do not answer Ilya; that distractor is then excluded only by inference. Key's 'not about next year' also asserts Whitby is next year, which lines 19-20 never state.
Line 21 'perished into something like a dried leaf' supports dry and crumbly; dominant-sense and other distractors excluded; hint points to the comparison without stating the meaning.

hintCore 'She names a stop and then a destination' describes the key's shape (warehouse, then shops) so the key can be picked from the options without reading; also the tag en-relation-word-flipped on 'She said she did not really know' names no relation word - the mistake is over-reading her hedge 'she thought' (line 25).
Lines 26-27 'laughed as well, slightly after her' supports a delayed, preoccupied laugh; distractors excluded by lines 23-28 as executions state; hint points at the qualifying words.

walkScript calls the cardigan 'a stranger's' - line 13 says only she 'had left in Year Four', nothing says Reuben did not know her; hintCore 'Two named jumpers' also miscounts, as line 13 item is a cardigan. Key itself checks against lines 11-14 and 29-34.
hintCore 'The last three words of line 36 matter most' is false: line 36 is 'opening it.' (two words); 'without' is on line 35. Key and distractors otherwise check.
passageRef missing (row cannot show its passage); distractor executions are also null.

hintCore 'He gives a day and a thing they escape' maps one-to-one onto the key (Monday + miss spellings) - coaching by shape. Tag en-relation-word-flipped on 'already been cleared by somebody else' also names no relation word in line 40.
hintCore 'She lifts it out, so it is a thing, not a coating' explicitly rules out the dominant-sense distractor the item exists to test - it does the vocabulary work for the child (R572 coaching).
Line 48 'longer than the answer needed' plus line 49 folding it away supports disbelief that she lets stand; distractor executions check; hint directs to her next action without stating it.

Key 'We get no thoughts from him' is false: lines 31-32 give what Reuben knew and why ('he knew the shape of the capitals his mum used'). hintCore 'Look for his hands' names the one word only the key carries (coaching); walkScript lists 'laughing late' as hands.
passageRef missing (row cannot show its passage); distractor executions are also null.

walkScript says line 1 'gives the one exception: it was very large' - 'except that it was very large' is on line 2, and 'night and morning' is lines 2-3, not 'at line 2' alone. Key and distractors check.
Lines 6-7 'had not bestowed one thought on Marley, since ... that afternoon'; negation, in-span and not-stated distractors excluded as executions state; hint targets the negation trap only.

'That' at line 15 points back to the whole preceding sentence, which begins with the hair 'curiously stirred, as if by breath or hot air' (line 14); under that reading the hair distractor is a defensible part-answer, and the execution/walkScript 'not to the hair' assert an antecedent the text does not fix.
Execution on 'He let go of the key' cites 'True at line 20'; 'the key he had relinquished' is on line 21 (walkScript repeats line 20 for it). Key and order otherwise check.
Line 23 'pause, with a moment's irresolution' supports indecision; built-from-parts, emotion and in-span distractors excluded; hint (deed or state) helps without naming the key.

hintCore 'Two of these only list the noises' eliminates two of three distractors outright, leaving the key against a flame option that is not a noise - coaching. Also lines 60-66 hold two noises (bells, then clanking), so 'the second noise' is ambiguous; the flame execution carries a malformed fragment ('own. Scrooge was not a man...').

Distractor 'Finding all the rooms in order, just as before' is supported by line 32 'All as they should be' and line 36 'Lumber-room as usual' - it is a true account of what he is doing (outcome rather than search), so the key is not the only defensible answer.

hintCore 'One of these says it was his custom. Line 39 does not.' points to the exact clause that is the key ('which was not his custom') - coaching. walkScript/execution also assert gown and nightcap are 'what he does every night', which the passage never states.
Lines 55-56 'a disused bell ... for some purpose now forgotten' supports the key; in-span, literal and draught distractors excluded; hint targets the draught distractor only.
Lines 69-70 'the dying flame leaped up ... and fell again'; ghost/door attribute-transfer, figurative cry and Scrooge's colour excluded as executions state; hint helps without naming the key.

Tag en-vocab-built-from-parts on 'Careful about every word he uses' does not name the mistake: its execution says it comes from 'cautious, a word it resembles in form' - a lookalike, not word parts. Key otherwise correct for line 78.
passageRef missing (row cannot show its passage).
Line 5 'scratch himself anywhere he pleased with any leg'; tail, out-of-window lap and not-stated race excluded; hint narrows to legs without giving the key.

Key 'The creature they took for dead' is inaccurate: only the boy calls him dead (line 12); the mother says 'Perhaps he isn't really dead' (line 13) and the man says he was not dead (line 15). A careful reader can reject the key on that word.
Line 15 'not dead but half choked'; negation, after-event and mother's words (line 13) excluded; hint points at the small word without naming the key.

Tag en-vocab-form-lookalike on 'So that he could go on and do something' misfits: its execution says it is the same word in 'in order to', while the tag hint tells the child to check it is not the same word. walkScript 'Everything near it is about his body' is also untrue (cotton wool, running round the table).
hintCore 'Two of these are things that happened, not reasons' eliminates two of three distractors outright, leaving the key against one motive-invention option - coaching.

Execution on 'He sat on all of their laps' claims 'line 34 answers the stem' and quotes 'Teddy went to bed Rikki-tikki climbed up too. But' - that is another distractor's content; the answer is lines 35-36.
Execution on 'A garden that somebody keeps tidy for him' says 'only half cultivated, so nobody is keeping it' - half cultivated means half of it is kept; the exclusion should rest on 'for him'.
passageRef missing (row cannot show its passage).
Line 54 'I am a stranger here. Who is Nag?' supports newcomer sense; stranger-danger, strange+er and in-span distractors excluded; hint targets one distractor only.

Execution on 'Because they had already told him about the baby' claims line 55 answers the stem by quoting 'Darzee and his wife only cowered down in the' - that is the restatement used by the literal-lookalike distractor, not the reason (the hiss, lines 55-56).
Lines 64-65 'Look, and be afraid!' gives the purpose; literal, in-span hood and invented warning excluded; hint directs without naming the key.

Execution on 'The writer says each time that Rikki-tikki is only proving the rule' says lines 39 and 68 are 'left without comment', but line 39 ('because every well-brought-up mongoose...') and line 68 ('it is impossible for a mongoose...') are the writer explicitly tying his act to the rule - the execution is false and the distractor is partly defensible.
